strengths: The virtual-correspondence construction is an original and useful practical approach to difficult three-view geometry. Generating correspondences from point coordinates and reusing established 5-point/6-point and P3P solvers makes the method substantially simpler to implement than specialized algebraic or homotopy-based alternatives.

The calibrated results demonstrate a meaningful accuracy–runtime trade-off. On PhotoTourism, 4p3v(M±δ)+R+F achieves AUC@10 of 70.47 at 75.78 ms, compared with 70.54 at 105.50 ms for 5pt+P3P (Table 2). The cheaper 4p3v(M)+R+F also outperforms the dedicated HC baseline in both accuracy and runtime. These supported practical gains favor acceptance.

The experimental support is substantial: PhotoTourism and Cambridge Landmarks, two RANSAC frameworks, fixed-iteration runtime curves, noise and outlier experiments, and refinement/perturbation ablations. Hyperparameters are selected on a held-out scene. Supplementary evaluation using the worst error across all camera pairs strengthens the evidence beyond the main averaged metric.
weaknesses: The shared-focal-length extension is less convincingly validated. In Table 3, 4p3vf(M) achieves AUC@10 of 49.88 versus 56.79 for 6pt+P3P, with similar runtime; the best learned variant remains less accurate and substantially slower. No focal-length estimation errors or direct accuracy comparison with existing 4p3vf homotopy solvers are reported. The results establish an efficient four-point approximation, but provide incomplete evidence for reliable joint pose and calibration recovery.

The approximation has significant, insufficiently characterized failure regimes. Lemma 1 bounds virtual-correspondence error by triangle extent, which does not establish small pose error or numerical stability. Figure 10 shows a substantial error floor even without measurement noise, and the manuscript acknowledges deterioration with small overlap. Results stratified by depth variation, baseline, or triangle geometry would better establish when the approach is dependable.

The learned component adds little demonstrated practical value after refinement. For example, PhotoTourism AUC@10 is 69.88 for 4p3v(L)+R versus 69.90 for 4p3v(M)+R, while runtime increases from 74.94 to 297.88 ms. Additionally, Eq. (2), as written, is a signed residual rather than a nonnegative Sampson loss; minimizing it need not favor epipolar consistency. This is a technical specification and reproducibility issue for the auxiliary learning contribution.

Baseline reporting needs reconciliation. The main text states that the oracle version of [35] performs worse than the proposed oracle, whereas Table 7 and Section 9.7 report the opposite after modifying RANSAC termination. Footnote 6 acknowledges this discrepancy, but the modification is not specified sufficiently for reproduction. Exact inlier thresholds are also missing. These are correctable reporting limitations, rather than reasons to dismiss the supported calibrated contribution.
